land.text: 'present-day Essex, Hertfordshire, and Suffolk, including parts of Greater London' on the north side of the Thames estuary; only Essex is drawn, because the Catuvellauni and Iceni dossiers hold the others

successors.note: 'finally conquered by either Tasciovanus or his son Cunobelinus', 'a few years later' than Dubnovellaunus (c. 10-5 BC); the Trinovantes page gives no year.

capitals.name: Camulodunum (Colchester)
capitals.note: Addedomarus took power 'c. 20-15 BC' and moved the capital to Camulodunum (modern Colchester); the page gives no coordinates. Before Caesar the capital 'was probably at Braughing' in Hertfordshire (not drawn, no earlier capital entry).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Essex, the core of the page's 'Essex, Hertfordshire, and Suffolk'. About 3.5 thousand km2 by the gazetteer. The page gives no frontier and no change of shape before the conquest.

region.text: 'present-day Essex, Hertfordshire, and Suffolk, including parts of Greater London' on the north side of the Thames estuary; only Essex is drawn, because the Catuvellauni and Iceni dossiers hold the others

ledger.note: 54 BC: first historical record. 'Shortly before Julius Caesar's invasion of Britain in 55 and 54 BC' the Trinovantes were considered 'the most powerful tribe in Britain'. Mandubracius, son of the king Imanuentius, 'fled to the protection of Caesar in Gaul' and was restored in Caesar's second expedition (no year on the page). The date is the first mention, not a founding.
c. 20-15 BC: Addedomarus took power and 'moved the capital to Camulodunum'. The page gives the range, not a year; 20 BC is its start.

region.text: 'present-day Essex, Hertfordshire, and Suffolk, including parts of Greater London' on the north side of the Thames estuary; only Essex is drawn, because the Catuvellauni and Iceni dossiers hold the others

ledger.note: Conquest by the Catuvellauni, page silent on the year. Tasciovanus issued coins from Camulodunum 'c. 10 BC', 'suggesting that he conquered the Trinovantes', but was 'soon forced to withdraw'; Dubnovellaunus ruled 'c. 10-5 BC'; the tribe was 'finally conquered by either Tasciovanus or his son Cunobelinus' 'a few years later'. 9 is the year the Catuvellauni dossier gives for Cunobelinus's succession, a bridge.

sources.title: Trinovantes
sources.note: Territory, Caesar's mention in 55 and 54 BC, Addedomarus and the move to Camulodunum, Dubnovellaunus, the Catuvellaunian conquest; no year for the conquest, nothing on AD 43.

notes: The counterpart of the catuvellauni dossier's gain of Camulodunum (conf 1, year 9). One page opened. The page gives no year for the conquest, no extent, and no date after AD 60 (it says the Trinovantes 'participated in Boudica's revolt against the Roman Empire in 60 AD', outside this dossier's life; the iceni dossier carries the revolt with 'Trinovantes' as a named belligerent). The page does not mention the invasion of AD 43 or the colonia at Colchester. Wikidata id unknown. Gazetteer: Camulodunum, Braughing are not place names (Colchester is).
